narration.text: On March eighteenth, nineteen thirty-seven, David J. Price arrived in New London, Texas. By then, everyone had a theory.
A leak. A spark. A simple chain of events.
Price wasn't interested in the clean version. He wanted the part the wreckage could actually prove. And one piece of it was clear.
The ignition appears to have started near the manual-training shop, where electrical equipment was running. That mattered.
But it wasn't the hardest question. Something else had already happened beneath the school.
Gas had accumulated in the dead space under the floor.
The source of that gas? That was different. After the hearings, the inspections, the technical work, Price still wouldn't pretend certainty. His report said it plainly.
It had not been possible to establish definitely where the accumulation came from.
That restraint is the story. Not what investigators guessed. What the evidence would let them say.
